read_scope: All 65 assigned complete Statement/Definition/Example/Statement-refuted/Remarks bodies and relevant full proofs; the 16–39 base-b/RQMC subjects were individually tested on all flagged worksheet axes.

items.review: Absolute expectation differences are bounded by 2M times event-supremum TV, and by M for nonnegative functions; neither bound characterizes TV equality.
The supplied measurable likelihood with finite positive evidence defines a posterior, and the declared metric chain assigns discrepancy labels without a recovery equivalence.
The metric triangle inequality bounds a finite chain; a bound on its endpoint distance does not characterize the intermediate points or attain equality.
The explicit identifiable three-outcome experiment has two equal modes, and the one-mode proxy has TV liminf at least one half; no characterization of Laplace accuracy is claimed.
The fixed correlated target has marginal variances one, while the unique independent ELBO optimizer has variances three quarters; this is a counterexample rather than an equivalence.
The two finite laws have matching means and variances but exact posterior mass 3/5 and synthetic posterior mass 1/2; moment matching is not a characterization of posterior equality.
The full laws distinguish the binary parameter but the nonconstant W-summary has Bernoulli(1/2) law at both labels; the item disproves the proposed implication.
The identity-summary example computes exact TV distance 23/85 at tolerance 3/5; it gives one witness, not necessary and sufficient tolerance conditions.
The Gaussian summary density is defined on positive-definite covariances, with unavailable finite plug-in output on singular covariance; no Gaussianity equivalence for actual summaries is asserted.
The binding definition explicitly identifies injectivity of the relevant law map with identifiability of the parameter, in addition to defining the lexicographic minimizer.
Two centered vectors in dimension two give covariance 2vv^T and an explicit nonzero null direction; no converse covariance classification is stated.
Compactness and continuity imply a nonempty compact argmin and unique lexicographically least minimizer; the conclusion is not asserted to imply compactness or continuity.

The procedure returns unavailable for a non-positive-definite sample covariance and otherwise evaluates the Gaussian density by its unique Cholesky factor; no correctness equivalence is separately asserted.
The remark contrasts a random finite plug-in value with the ideal density and notes singular two-simulation outputs; it states neither necessary nor sufficient conditions for consistency.
The Bernoulli summary gives zero mass to (1/4,3/4), while its positive-variance Gaussian gives positive mass there; the verification establishes inequality of these laws.
The four-corner model has population covariance I_2 and random sample covariances zero or a displayed rank-one matrix; every two-simulation output is unavailable.
The Definition assigns Haar contrasts, finite ANOVA projections and squared component norms; it postpones complete orthogonal decomposition to a separate result.
The digit-cylinder construction yields independent uniform digit streams and permutations from one uniform variable; the claim does not characterize all possible constructions.
The lambda-net label is defined by the elementary-interval count condition at total depth m-t, counting ordered multiplicities.
The Definition identifies marginal uniformity with each listed point having normalized Lebesgue law, while separately requiring a declared discrepancy condition for an RQMC design.
The finite span of b-adic box indicators is dense in Borel L2; the theorem is a density assertion, not a characterization of bases or measures.
Continuous mixed derivatives imply the displayed geometric ANOVA energy bound; existence of such a bound is not asserted to recover derivatives.
The Definition constructs digits using independent node permutations indexed by original input prefixes; it does not characterize every marginally uniform randomization.
The complete orthonormal Haar family gives the L2 expansion and Parseval variance sum under Countable Choice; no converse characterization is stated in this item.
Marginal uniformity gives finite-rule unbiasedness by linearity without point independence; unbiasedness for one fixed integrand is not claimed to imply uniform marginals.
The Definition applies common independent digit shifts modulo b and fixes the output value-one null representative; it does not characterize all dependent point arrays.
IID full-set replicate estimates with finite variance give an unbiased variance estimator for the replicate mean; unbiasedness alone does not characterize independent randomizations.
The node-permutation scramble yields uniform marginals and preserves elementary net counts almost surely; those two properties do not characterize its entire randomization law.
The common digital shift yields uniform marginals and preserves the input net almost surely; these conclusions are not a converse characterization of digital shifts.
The Studentized replicate statistic converges to N(0,1) at fixed rule under positive finite variance and AC; a limit law does not characterize all admissible finite replicate laws.
The nested-scramble variance equals its ANOVA gain series; this identity is asserted for the specified construction rather than as an equivalence defining randomization laws.
Expanding the product of prefix indicators gives the alternating subset formula for each gain; no converse condition for being a scrambled net is stated.
The general-net gain vanishes at low total depth and is otherwise bounded by lambda times b to the stated exponent; the bounds do not characterize net quality.
The zero-net gain is bounded by (b/(b-1)) to min(m,d-1); the proof gives sufficient net hypotheses, not a converse classification.
Continuous mixed derivatives and fixed net quality give the variance rate along n=lambda b^m; the item does not recover smoothness from an observed rate.
The zero-net variance is bounded by the sharp gain constant times sigma squared over n, and then by e times that ratio; neither bound is a characterization of f.
The two-point linear-integrand example computes variance 1/96 and shows why replicate variance estimation needs R at least two; it contains no equivalence assertion.
The skewed two-replicate example computes coverage 98/2500 for a nominal 95 percent interval; its exact calculation does not characterize all Student coverage failures.
The two randomizations have the same uniform marginals and exact net counts but variances 1/48 and 1/96; this is a counterexample to determination by those properties.
The linear integrand has the smooth rate whereas x to minus three quarters is integrable with infinite second moment; these two examples are not a smoothness characterization.
The digital-net Definition requires both a generated point set and the exact net counting property; arbitrary generator matrices are expressly insufficient.
The upper-anchor variation is the finite sum of Vitali variations over nonempty upper faces; it defines a quantity rather than asserting an equivalent regularity condition.
Bounded coordinatewise monotonicity implies Riemann integrability; the Darboux criterion used in the proof is a supplier equivalence, not a converse monotonicity claim.
The lower-anchor Definition assigns zero to terms with a varied side of length zero and otherwise sums Vitali face variations; it asserts no two-way regularity criterion.
The digital branch explicitly returns net check passed exactly when every elementary interval count equals p to t.
The smooth mixed-derivative lemma computes upper-anchor variation as the sum of face integrals of absolute mixed derivatives; it does not characterize smoothness from finite variation.
The finite summation-by-parts identity yields an anchored discrepancy bound for every node-containing grid and finite HK variation; it does not give a converse regularity criterion.
Vanishing star discrepancy implies convergence of quadrature for all bounded Riemann integrands; this item does not state the converse characterization of uniform distribution.
Finite upper-anchor HK variation implies boundedness and Riemann integrability by a reflected monotone decomposition; Riemann integrability is not claimed to imply finite HK variation.
The Koksma-Hlawka inequality bounds deterministic quadrature error by star discrepancy times upper-anchor variation; equality or a converse characterization is not claimed.
The explicit diagonal four-node lattice has good one-coordinate projections but fails the two-dimensional net count and has star discrepancy at least 1/4.
Six cannot equal a power of two, yet the rank-one lattice with generator (1,1) is admissible; this is a size-restriction example rather than a characterization of all quadrature rules.
The function xy and one node give variation 3, discrepancy 7/8 and error 1/8; these exact computations verify an inequality without an equivalence claim.
The inverse-CDF proof explicitly uses the equivalence between g(u) at most x and x to minus two at most 1-u for x at least one.
The binary64 example computes exact dot product 3 and rounded result 2, with absolute error one within the gamma bound; no condition-number equivalence is claimed.
The fixed bootstrap realization separates sampling error -1/4 from simulation error 1/8 and verifies the conditional law; it makes no bootstrap-validity equivalence.
The three-element orbit has p-value 1/3 whereas the realized four-transform formula gives 2/5; the item makes no characterization of finite-B validity.
The one-step Euler example computes persistent bias 10-(5/2)e squared and path variance 36/M; it does not characterize consistency of arbitrary discretizations.
Three independent-rule outputs give mean 8/15 and estimated mean variance 7/900; the verification is arithmetic with fixed data, not an equivalence about confidence coverage.
The Rademacher errors U and V=U have squared sum expectation four but variance-only sum two; their covariance supplies the missing term without a general equivalence assertion.
The MSE identity includes total squared bias and pairwise covariances, with equality to the variance sum exactly when their combined correction is zero.
IID finite-variance replicates give an unbiased variance estimate for the mean; the item does not claim unbiasedness characterizes IID inputs.
An IID sequence with positive finite variance gives the normalized-sum CLT under AC; the normal limit is not asserted to characterize IID laws.
The coupled discontinuous-payoff hierarchy has bias order one and correction-variance order one half; the example provides a witness, not an equivalence of regularity and rates.
The supplied-measure Gaussian lemma transfers compact Riemann integrals and evaluates Gaussian mass and moments; it asserts no construction or characterization of the supplied measures.
